recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future redesign of Condition.clinicalStatus value-set adequacy should be handled under a finalized later tracker such as FHIR-54841, not by reopening FHIR-14874.
issue_request: FHIR-14874 is a Published Patient Care STU3 Condition issue with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. The issue discussion raised broader concerns that Condition.clinicalStatus should not be constrained to the existing clinical status value set, but the final voted resolution was specifically to remove the well-controlled and poorly-controlled codes from the existing Condition clinical status value set.
initial_application: Commit f4005f37a69d8556e2141831d1593747b2319994 applied GF#14874 by deleting the well-controlled and poorly-controlled concepts from source/condition/codesystem-condition-clinical.xml. Later commit cccb69d8142e7ec5234dde242ca3da5d556591f5 removed the residual comment about those statuses, and 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 externalized UTG terminology content from the core build.
additional_context: FHIR-13026 is the earlier Published issue that added the controlled-status codes and is superseded by this seed. Current source/fhir.ini lists Condition as an active, approved resource; source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml binds Condition.clinicalStatus to ValueSet/condition-clinical; and source/condition/valueset-condition-clinical.xml composes that value set from the THO condition-clinical code system. The local THO package lists active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, resolved, and unknown, but not well-controlled or poorly-controlled. FHIR-54841 is a later Waiting for Input issue about broader value-set adequacy and is not final source-edit scope for this run.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because no source edit is needed for FHIR-14874. The current core source and terminology dependency already reflect the final applied decision.
